title: Historical baseline rollforward and priority-smoke CI hook for fast regression gating
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce noisy CI cycles and catch prompt-set regressions earlier by maintaining a rolling historical baseline and exposing a lightweight priority-smoke CI hook that runs in pull requests. This PR introduces a rollforward-able baseline snapshot format, a prioritized sampling algorithm for producing tiny smoke cohorts, an integration in the eval-runner to compute stabilized delta metrics (win-rate with bootstrap intervals and length-normalized perplexity proxy), and a CI adapter that fails fast on statistically significant regression signals while allowing configurable escalation. Key behaviors: 1) Baseline snapshots are stored as anchored JSONL with metadata (model version, commit, timestamp, aggregated metrics); 2) Rollforward workflow: when a PR updates a prompt set or model scoring, the CI compares the PR run to the latest baseline and if changes are benign the snapshot is rollforwarded automatically with a short TTL; 3) Priority-smoke sampler selects N=150 high-impact prompts using a combination of recent-failure weight, user-frequency weight, and semantic diversity hashing to maximize early-detection power; 4) Metrics: primary signal is weighted pairwise win-rate with bootstrap CI and actionable effect-size thresholds, secondary signals include response-length-normalized score and top-k token-shift; 5) CI hook modes: fast-smoke (PR-level, ~3-5m), expanded-smoke (pre-merge gated run, ~15-20m), and backfill (nightly full baseline recompute). Backfill triggers remedial guidance and automatic rollback candidates when large historical drift is detected. Compatibility: integrates with existing eval-runner, supports existing cohort/spec yaml, and can be toggled per-repo via eval-harness config. Migration notes: existing baseline format is supported as read-only; operators must run `scripts/baseline-upgrade` once per workspace to enable rollforward metadata. Rationale: many regressions in our deployment pipeline are surfaced only after full-house evals; a statistically-driven tiny-smoke approach yields much faster feedback with low cost and higher signal-to-noise. This PR bundles implementation, docs, and CI wiring so reviewers can test end-to-end in feature branches.

review_comments: Sanjay: Can we make the default priority-smoke cohort size configurable via project config instead of hardcoding N=150? I want to use 50 for some low-cost repos. Author response: added config path `eval.priority_smoke.size` and doc example.

Ruth: The bootstrap CI sometimes produced wide intervals on small cohorts; can we include a fallback deterministic delta (median difference) to avoid flapping? Author response: implemented median-delta fallback and added a unit test and a flag `--deterministic-fallback`.

Jonas: Suggest to gate rollforward by a manual approval for high-impact prompt sets flagged in metadata. Author response: added `impact_level` metadata and default requires approval for impact_level >= high.
CI: first run failed on lint in snapshot.py, autorun fixed by commit d2b8f22 which tightened whitespace and imports, subsequent rerun passed.
release_notes: Adds historical baseline snapshot format and lightweight priority-smoke CI hook for rapid prompt-set regression detection. Includes sampler, metrics, CI action, operator docs, and migration script. Configurable cohort size and impact gating.
